lessons.title: Notre voyage en français
lessons.oneGoal: Students reflect on their French learning journey throughout the year

opening.activity: Show calendar from September to now. Say 'Regardons notre voyage!' Use hand gesture of traveling/walking to introduce 'voyage'. Point to different months and ask students what they remember.

main.activity: Journey Timeline - Create a visual timeline of the school year on the floor using masking tape. Students walk along the timeline, stopping at different months to share memories of French learning. Teacher adds pictures/artifacts at each stop.

closing.activity: Journey Reflection - Students sit in circle and each shares one word (in French or English) to describe their French learning journey this year.

lessons.realWorldConnection: People look back on their year to see how much they've grown and learned - like looking through photo albums with family

lessons.title: Nos premiers mots français
lessons.oneGoal: Students revisit and celebrate the first French words they learned

opening.activity: Show timeline from yesterday and point to September. Ask 'Quels étaient nos premiers mots?' Show 'premier' with finger gesture (number 1) and 'célébrer' with clapping.

main.activity: First Words Treasure Hunt - Hide early vocabulary cards around the room (bonjour, au revoir, merci, oui, non, etc.). Students find cards and try to remember learning these words. Create a 'First Words Hall of Fame' poster together.

closing.activity: First Words Celebration - Class says each first word together with original actions/gestures. End with appreciation: 'Nous avons bien appris!'

lessons.realWorldConnection: We remember our 'firsts' - first words, first steps, first day of school - they're special milestones

lessons.title: Chansons et comptines préférées
lessons.oneGoal: Students revisit and perform favorite French songs and rhymes from the year

opening.activity: Hum a familiar French tune from early in the year. Ask students to identify it. Introduce 'chanson' with singing gesture and 'comptine' with rhythmic clapping.

main.activity: Musical Memory Lane - Vote on favorite songs/rhymes from the year. Perform top 3-4 choices with original actions. Students can suggest new movements or variations. Create a 'Greatest Hits' list.

closing.activity: Song Circle - Sit in circle and each student hums or sings one line from their personal favorite French song from the year.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Music helps us remember and connects us to happy memories - like family songs or lullabies from childhood

lessons.title: Histoires que nous aimons
lessons.oneGoal: Students revisit favorite French stories and books from throughout the year

opening.activity: Show stack of French books from the year. Ask 'Quelle histoire préférez-vous?' Show 'aimer' with heart gesture over chest.

main.activity: Story Museum - Set up stations with different beloved books from the year. Students rotate through stations, looking at books and sharing memories of each story. Vote on class favorite and reread together.

closing.activity: Story Sharing Circle - Each student shows their favorite page from the winning book and says why they like it (can use English if needed).

lessons.realWorldConnection: Favorite stories stay with us and shape how we see the world - like bedtime stories that become lifelong memories

lessons.title: Nos réussites en français
lessons.oneGoal: Students identify and celebrate specific French learning achievements

opening.activity: Show examples of student work from September vs. now. Point out growth and say 'Regardez vos réussites!' Show 'fier' with proud posture and big smile.

main.activity: Achievement Gallery Walk - Display student work from throughout the year. Students walk around and place gold stars on work that shows their growth or makes them proud. Discuss what makes each piece special.

closing.activity: Pride Circle - Each student shares one thing they're proud of learning in French this year. Class responds with 'Bravo!' and applause.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Recognizing our achievements helps build confidence and motivation - like celebrating learning to ride a bike or swim

lessons.title: Défis surmontés ensemble
lessons.oneGoal: Students reflect on challenges they overcame in French learning

opening.activity: Remind students of early year challenges (silent period, new sounds, etc.). Show 'défi' with barrier gesture, then 'surmonter' with climbing over motion.

main.activity: Challenge Champions - Discuss common challenges from the year (pronunciation, understanding, participating). Students share how they or classmates helped overcome these. Create a 'Challenge Champions' poster showing strategies.

closing.activity: Strength Circle - Each student names one way they helped themselves or a classmate overcome a French challenge this year.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Everyone faces challenges, and overcoming them makes us stronger - like learning to ride a bike or make new friends

lessons.title: Amis et moments spéciaux
lessons.oneGoal: Students reflect on friendships and special moments in French class

opening.activity: Show photos of students working together during the year. Ask 'Qui sont vos amis en français?' Show 'spécial' with hands making heart shape.

main.activity: Memory Sharing Circle - Students take turns sharing a special moment with a friend in French class. Could be helping each other, laughing together, or collaborative successes. Create memory cards to keep.

closing.activity: Friendship Appreciation - Students give compliments to classmates about their French learning journey: 'Merci [name] pour...' with teacher translation support.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Learning is more meaningful when we share it with friends - like playing games or exploring new places together

lessons.title: Créations dont nous sommes fiers
lessons.oneGoal: Students revisit and celebrate creative work produced throughout the year

opening.activity: Set up a mini art gallery with student work from the year. Say 'Voici nos créations!' Show 'fier' with proud stance and big smile.

main.activity: Artist Gallery Walk - Students walk through display of their creative work (art, writing, projects) from the year. Each student chooses their proudest creation to present to the class with simple explanation.

closing.activity: Creator's Circle - Each student holds their chosen creation and receives applause from classmates. End with group cheer: 'Nous sommes des artistes!'

lessons.realWorldConnection: Artists and creators look back at their work to see their journey - like looking through a photo album or memory book

lessons.title: Commencer notre portfolio
lessons.oneGoal: Students begin organizing their year's work into a meaningful portfolio

opening.activity: Show an example portfolio. Explain 'portfolio' as a special book of our best work. Show 'organiser' by sorting papers into groups.

main.activity: Portfolio Organization - Students begin sorting their work into categories (writing, art, photos, certificates). Start organizing chronologically or by theme. Teacher circulates to help with decision-making.

closing.activity: Organization Share - Students show their portfolio start to a partner and explain their organization system.

lessons.realWorldConnection: People create portfolios to show their best work and growth over time - like photo albums or memory books

lessons.title: Choisir nos meilleurs exemples
lessons.oneGoal: Students select their best work samples for portfolio inclusion

opening.activity: Continue portfolio work from yesterday. Show 'choisir' with selection gestures. Discuss what makes work 'meilleur' - effort, growth, pride, learning shown.

main.activity: Best Work Selection - Students review all their work and select pieces that show: 1) Their best effort, 2) Their growth, 3) Their learning, 4) Work they're proud of. Use simple criteria checklist to guide decisions.

closing.activity: Selection Reflection - Students place selected work in portfolios and share with partner why each piece was chosen.

lessons.realWorldConnection: We choose our best examples when applying for jobs or showing our abilities - like when we show our best drawings to family

lessons.title: Raconter notre histoire d'apprentissage
lessons.oneGoal: Students create narratives explaining their learning journey and growth

opening.activity: Look at completed portfolio sections. Explain that now we tell the 'histoire' of our learning. Show 'raconter' with storytelling gestures.

main.activity: Learning Story Creation - Students create their learning story using template: 'Au début...', 'Puis...', 'Maintenant...', 'Dans le futur...' Can be written, drawn, or recorded orally with teacher support.

closing.activity: Story Preview - 3-4 students share one sentence from their learning story. Others listen and appreciate.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Everyone has a learning story - how we grew and changed over time - like telling family about school or sharing adventures

lessons.title: Partager avec nos familles
lessons.oneGoal: Students prepare to share their portfolios and growth with families

opening.activity: Show completed portfolios with pride. Explain that we will 'partager' with 'famille'. Show 'montrer' with presentation gestures.

main.activity: Family Presentation Prep - Students practice showing their portfolios and telling their learning story. Practice key French phrases to share with families: 'Voici mon travail', 'Je suis fier de...', 'J'ai appris...'

closing.activity: Practice Partner Share - Students practice their family presentation with a classmate, giving each other encouragement.

lessons.realWorldConnection: We share our achievements and growth with people who care about us - like showing report cards or art projects at home

lessons.title: Célébrer nos progrès
lessons.oneGoal: Students participate in a celebration of their French learning progress

opening.activity: Enter classroom decorated for celebration. Announce 'Aujourd'hui nous célébrons!' Show 'grandir' with growing gesture from small to tall.

main.activity: Progress Celebration Festival - Multiple celebration stations: 1) Portfolio viewing, 2) French song performance, 3) Achievement certificate ceremony, 4) Reflection sharing circle. Families invited if possible.

closing.activity: Celebration Circle - Everyone (students, families, teacher) stands in circle for final appreciation and group photo.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Celebrations mark important milestones and achievements in our lives - like birthdays, graduations, or family accomplishments

lessons.title: Regarder vers l'avenir
lessons.oneGoal: Students set goals and express hopes for continued French learning

opening.activity: Look at timeline from Lesson 1, but extend it into the future. Show 'avenir' by pointing ahead, 'espoir' with hopeful gesture, 'continuer' with ongoing motion.

main.activity: Future French Dreams - Students create simple goals for continued French learning: 'L'année prochaine, je veux...' Support with pictures and simple phrases. Share hopes for Grade 2 French adventures.

closing.activity: Future Circle - Each student shares one hope for their French learning future. Teacher responds with encouragement and belief in their continued growth.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Setting goals helps us continue growing and reaching for new achievements - like planning summer activities or dreaming about what we want to be when we grow up

lessons.title: Jeux de révision amusants
lessons.oneGoal: Students play engaging games reviewing vocabulary and concepts from the year

opening.activity: Celebrate completing all core lessons! Show game materials and say 'Maintenant nous jouons!' Show 'amusant' with big smile and playful gesture.

main.activity: Game Station Carnival - Set up 4 stations: 1) Memory matching with year's vocabulary, 2) Charades with French actions, 3) Musical French freeze dance, 4) Simple French bingo. Rotate every 6-7 minutes.

closing.activity: Game Champions Circle - Everyone gets appreciation for game participation. Vote on favorite game to play again tomorrow.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Playing games with what we've learned makes knowledge stick and brings joy - like family game nights or playground games

lessons.title: Spectacle de talents français
lessons.oneGoal: Students showcase their French abilities through performances or presentations

opening.activity: Set up performance area like a talent show. Explain 'spectacle' with stage gestures and 'talent' by pointing to students with pride.

main.activity: French Talent Showcase - Students choose how to showcase their French: singing, reciting, storytelling, demonstrating vocabulary, or simple conversations. Everyone performs something, however small.

closing.activity: Standing Ovation - After all performances, everyone stands for appreciation of courage and French growth shown by all participants.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Talent shows let us share our abilities and celebrate what makes each person special - like school concerts or family performances

lessons.title: Lettres à nous-mêmes
lessons.oneGoal: Students write letters to their future selves about their French learning experience

opening.activity: Show example of a letter. Explain writing to 'futur' self - the student they will be in Grade 2. Show timeline extending into next year.

main.activity: Future Self Letters - Students write simple letters to their Grade 2 selves about French learning: what they learned, what they're proud of, advice for continuing. Use mix of French phrases and English as needed.

closing.activity: Letter Sealing Ceremony - Students seal letters in special envelopes to be opened at start of Grade 2 (with teacher coordination).

lessons.realWorldConnection: Writing to our future selves helps us remember important moments and lessons - like time capsules or diary entries

lessons.title: Cadeau pour la prochaine classe
lessons.oneGoal: Students create something helpful for next year's Grade 1 French students

opening.activity: Discuss how scary but exciting starting Grade 1 French was. Show 'cadeau' with giving gesture and explain creating something special for new students.

main.activity: Gift Creation Workshop - Students create welcome gifts for new Grade 1 French students: advice cards, welcome posters, recorded messages, or simple French phrase books. Focus on encouragement and support.

closing.activity: Gift Presentation - Students show their gifts and explain how they will help new French learners feel welcome and confident.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Helping others who are starting their journey is a way to give back and show growth - like big siblings helping little ones

lessons.title: Temps libre français
lessons.oneGoal: Students engage in free choice French activities based on their interests

opening.activity: Show choice menu of French activities. Explain 'temps libre' - time to choose what they want to do in French. Show 'intérêt' by asking about preferences.

main.activity: French Choice Time - Students choose from: French books, drawing with French labels, singing French songs, playing French games, or creating with French materials. Teacher supports all choices.

closing.activity: Choice Reflection - Students share what they chose and why. Appreciate the variety of interests and ways to enjoy French.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Having choices about what we do helps us feel ownership and enjoyment - like choosing what games to play or books to read

lessons.title: Au revoir et à bientôt!
lessons.oneGoal: Students celebrate the end of Grade 1 French and look forward to continuing

opening.activity: Gather in celebration circle. Explain this is 'au revoir' to Grade 1 French but 'à bientôt' because French learning continues. Show excitement for future.

main.activity: Final Celebration Festival - Multiple stations: memory book signing, photo taking, favorite activity reprises, future preview, and appreciation circle. End with group performance of favorite French song.

closing.activity: Final Circle - Everyone shares one word describing their Grade 1 French experience. End with group hug and 'À bientôt!' rather than goodbye.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Saying goodbye to one chapter means we're ready to start the next adventure - like finishing a good book and looking for the next one

familyConnections.unitLetter:
Chers parents et familles,

Nous sommes ravis de commencer notre nouvelle unité: "Notre année française"

Cette unité permettra à votre enfant de:
• Explorer des concepts importants en français
• Développer du vocabulaire en français
• Pratiquer de nouvelles compétences
• Faire des connexions avec la vie quotidienne

Quelques thèmes que nous explorerons:
Notre voyage en français, Nos premiers mots français, Chansons et comptines préférées, Histoires que nous aimons, Nos réussites en français

Comment vous pouvez aider à la maison:
• Demandez à votre enfant de partager ce qu'il/elle a appris
• Pratiquez le nouveau vocabulaire ensemble (voir la liste ci-jointe)
• Essayez les activités suggérées quand vous avez du temps
• Célébrez les efforts et les progrès, pas seulement les résultats

Il est normal et bénéfique que votre enfant mélange les langues à la maison.

N'hésitez pas à me contacter si vous avez des questions ou si vous souhaitez partager des ressources culturelles liées à cette unité.

Merci pour votre soutien continu dans l'apprentissage du français!

Cordialement,
[Nom de l'enseignant(e)]
